description: Change of use of retail premises (Use Class E (a)) to indoor gymnasium (Use Class E (d)) operating 24 hours Monday to Sunday and Bank holidays.
decision_conditions: The applicant has failed to demonstrate through appropriate locally specific evidence that retail or commercial demand no longer exists at the application premises or within the relevant part of Leytonstone District Centre. The recent closure of the former retailer, together with reliance upon nationwide store closures and general economic conditions, does not adequately evidence the local vacancy or commercial demand circumstances necessary to justify the proposed conversion of the established retail premises to leisure use. The proposal therefore fails to accord with the objectives of Policy 40 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

In the absence of a Noise Assessment and appropriate technical evidence addressing airborne and structure borne noise and vibration. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed 24 hour gymnasium, including its free weight, strength and functional training activities, would avoid unacceptable noise, vibration and general disturbance to adjoining residential occupiers. The proposal therefore fails to safeguard neighbouring residential amenity, contrary to Policies 44, 50 and 57 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

Having regard to the constrained and sensitive town centre location of the premises adjacent to the junction of High Road Leytonstone and Church Lane, the absence of an Outline Construction Logistics Plan and Delivery and Servicing Plan, including satisfactory refuse and recycling collection arrangements, means that the applicant has failed to demonstrate that construction, delivery, servicing and waste activities associated with the development can be undertaken safely and without unacceptable impacts upon the surrounding highway and its users. The proposal therefore fails to accord with Policies 63, 64 and 65 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

The applicant has failed to provide adequate secure and accessible cycle parking for staff and visitors in accordance with the minimum standards applicable to the proposed Use Class E(d) sports facility, and has failed to provide sufficient information regarding peak time visitor numbers to establish the level of short stay cycle parking required. The absence of identified long  and short stay cycle parking would fail to support sustainable and active modes of travel and would conflict with Policies 60 and 61 and Appendix 1 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Part 1 (2024).
